prō-pălam , adv.,
I.openly, publicly, notoriously, manifestly (class.): “minus jam furtificus sum: rapio propalam,” Plaut. Ep. 1, 1, 10 : signis propalam collocatis, * Cic. de Or. 1, 35, 161: “dicere,” Liv. 34, 33 : “obviam ire,” id. 3, 25 : “alii propalam, alii per occultum,” Tac. A. 6, 7 : “propalam aspici,” id. ib. 2, 39 : “timeo, ne hoc propalam fiat,” may become manifest, Plaut. Mil. 4, 8, 38 : propalam est, it is clear, manifest (post-class.), Ter. Maur. p. 2435 P.
From A Latin Dictionary (Charlton T. Lewis, Charles Short, Oxford, Clarendon Press, 1879)
